provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Care family batch. Smallest ticket in the family: booking, walk-in queue and the Google profile matter more than the site, so every add-on and product is priced low. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Walk-in hours, the current wait for each barber where the shop shares it, a join-the-queue button and a text when the chair is nearly ready
pageStructurePlus.why: Half of barbershop customers decide by the wait, not the price. A shop that shows its line wins the guy standing outside the one that doesn't.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Low, mid and high fades, skin fades, tapers, line-ups, crops and textured tops, each with a name, a short description and the clipper guard lengths the shop uses
pageStructurePlus.why: Most men can't describe the haircut they want. A style guide gives them the word to book, and fewer cuts go wrong in the chair.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Kids' pricing, the age the shop starts at, quiet hours for nervous or sensory-sensitive kids, and a first haircut certificate with a lock of hair
pageStructurePlus.why: Parents choose a barber on patience. The barbershop that says how it handles a nervous kid gets the whole family for years.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Monthly membership for a set number of haircuts or line-ups, beard work included or not, priority booking, and how to pause or cancel
pageStructurePlus.why: Regulars who get a fade every two weeks do the maths. A membership page turns that habit into steady monthly income for the barber.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Booth rent, what's included (chair, station, products, booking), shop hours, the vibe and a short application
pageStructurePlus.why: Barbershop owners are always filling a chair, and good barbers check the shop's online presence before they walk in to ask.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Wedding party haircuts and hot towel shaves in the shop or on location, group pricing, timing on the day and the deposit that holds it
pageStructurePlus.why: Grooms book barbers months ahead for the whole party. A clear groomsmen page turns a Saturday into a booked group.

designDirections.name: Chair Queue
designDirections.bestFor: One- and two-chair barbershops that need prices, a queue button and hours, not a portfolio
designDirections.headlineSample: Fades, beards and line-ups in {City}. Walk in or book.
designDirections.whyItFits: Cobalt & Butter's slab type feels like a hand-lettered shop window, and the stacked cards put the wait, the price and Book right under the thumb.

designDirections.name: Navy Chair
designDirections.bestFor: Multi-barber shops with a set menu, barber bios and both walk-ins and appointments
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Sage Spa, fails CTA contrast and reads as a quiet spa, not a barbershop. Navy & Brass has the classic barber-pole confidence and its brass Book button passes AA.

designDirections.name: Late Lounge
designDirections.bestFor: Upscale barber lounges selling hot towel shaves, memberships and a drink while you wait
designDirections.headlineSample: Hot towel shaves and precision cuts in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Obsidian Amber's dark ground and warm amber read like low lounge lighting, and the geometric display keeps it modern rather than costume vintage.

openers.line: The barbershop's Maps listing has good reviews and hours, but no website or booking link, so a guy in {City} searching for a fade near him has to call and hope someone hears the phone over the clippers.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website or booking button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what that button could open for the barbershop: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Booking app with no shop behind it
openers.line: Your bio goes straight into a booking app that lists cuts by name with no prices for kids or beard add-ons. New customers want to know what the barbershop charges before they pick a barber.
openers.hook: Tap their bio link and note what's missing: prices, add-ons, barber names, the address.
openers.linkLine: A barbershop page that shows the menu before the booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: The barbershop's listing says open till eight on Sundays but your last post says closed Sundays. One of those sends a customer to a locked door.
openers.hook: Compare their listing hours with their latest posts. Note any mismatch exactly.
openers.linkLine: A barbershop page with hours you can change by text: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened the barbershop's site on my phone and the haircut prices were a picture too small to read. Everybody booking a fade is on a phone.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The barbershop, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.angle: No idea how long the wait is
openers.line: People keep asking in your comments how long the wait is for walk-ins. A queue they can join from their phone would answer it before they drive over to the barbershop.
openers.hook: Look for 'how long's the wait' or 'are you busy' comments. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A barbershop page with a walk-in queue: {demo-link}

openers.line: The barbers' best fades and tapers are mixed in with memes and shop music clips. A cut gallery with each barber's work sorted would help customers choose a chair.
openers.hook: Pick one barber and one cut style they clearly own. Name both if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Each barber's cuts, sorted by style: {demo-link}

openers.line: A Google review says your barber was the first one who got a kid through a haircut without tears. That's the line that books every nervous parent in the neighbourhood.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about a barber, a kid's cut or the atmosphere. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Your reviews right beside the barbershop's Book button: {demo-link}

openers.line: The week before school starts, every parent wants a kids' haircut on the same Saturday. A booking page for the barbershop spreads that rush across the whole week.
openers.hook: Use this from late July to the end of August, or before school photos. Check their posts for a back-to-school mention.

openers.line: Sunday night is when guys realise they need a haircut before Monday's meeting. If the barbershop can't be booked then, they book whoever can.
openers.hook: Look for comments asking 'you open tomorrow?' late at night. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A barbershop that books on Sunday night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw the post about a barber chair for rent. Good barbers check how the shop looks online before they come in to talk booth rent.
openers.hook: Only if they posted 'chair available', 'booth rent' or 'now hiring barbers'. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A barbershop page with a rent-a-chair section: {demo-link}

openers.line: New apartments are filling up around {Neighborhood}, and every guy moving in is searching for a barber nearby. Right now the shop doesn't show up with prices and a booking link.
openers.hook: Check for new apartment buildings or a growing neighbourhood near the shop. Use the real name.
openers.linkLine: A barbershop page for the new neighbours: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your door says cash only and nothing online says what a cut and beard costs. A guy without cash finds out at the chair, which is awkward for the barber too.
openers.hook: Look for 'cash only' signs in their posts or reviews mentioning payment. Don't push card payments they don't want.
openers.linkLine: A barbershop menu with prices and payment info: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your barbers are licensed and good at what they do, and nothing online says so. A parent or a guy new to {City} wants to know that before he sits in a stranger's chair.
openers.hook: Look for licence certificates on the wall in posts or 'licensed barber' in bios. Never invent one.
openers.linkLine: Your barbers' bios and licensing, stated plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: The barbershop runs on regulars who've been coming for years, which is great. When one of them moves, the guy who'd replace him searches before he ever walks past.
openers.hook: Look for posts celebrating long-time customers or reviews saying 'been coming here for years'. Quote one.
openers.linkLine: Where a new barbershop customer would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} on your page is a clean cut, sharp line-up and all. Work like that should headline the barber's profile, not disappear by the weekend.
openers.hook: Pick the newest cut post and name it exactly: the style, the barber and anything distinctive.
openers.linkLine: That cut, at the top of the barber's profile: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} on the barbershop's page is a clean cut.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and only found the listing and the booking app. I put together a sample barbershop page with prices, a walk-in queue, a fade guide and a Book button, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case it got buried. Here's the sample barbershop site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It shows the menu with prices, a walk-in queue customers join from their phone, a fade style guide and each barber's chair. If it's not for you, just say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hey, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I set up websites and booking for barbershops here in {City}. I sent the shop a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"All good, I know you're cutting all day. Short version: I built a sample page for {Business Name} with prices, a walk-in queue and booking for each barber, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and price changes. For a shop your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Honestly, the booking and your Google profile do most of the work. The page just makes them look like one shop."
"Can I swing by on a slow morning this week? Ten minutes, I'll show you on my phone."

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start when it clears."

objections.objection: We're walk-in only, we don't need a website.
objections.handler: "That's fine, the page is built around walk-ins. It shows the wait and lets guys join the queue from their phone, so they show up when the chair's free."

objections.objection: The booking app is all we need.
objections.handler: "Keep it. This puts your prices, barbers and the fade guide in front of it and sends people into your booking app. Searchers find the shop, not just a listing inside an app."

objections.objection: Barbers come and go, I'd be updating it all the time.
objections.handler: "That's what the monthly care is for. A barber leaves or joins, you text me, the chair page changes that day."

objections.objection: Everybody here finds us by word of mouth.
objections.handler: "Word of mouth still ends with a search for the barbershop's name. The page makes sure the first thing they see is the right hours and a way to book."
"It's sized for a barbershop. {Build Range}, and for you about {Build Price}. That's a few weeks of a single chair's cuts, and it works every night the shop's closed."

email.subject: A page for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hey {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I set up booking pages for barbershops in {City}, and I made a sample for {Business Name}. I'll text you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm pulling the {Business Name} barbershop demo down Friday to clear space.

Want it left up? One word's fine.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner}, back-to-school and holiday weeks are coming, the two busiest stretches for barbers. Shops with online booking and a queue handle that rush calmer. Thought of you.

The sample's still here and the price hasn't moved. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a few weeks of one chair's cuts. A barbershop's ticket is the smallest in the family, so the build has to be too.
Lead with the booking setup and the Google profile; the page is the frame around them.
Price per barber chair page, not per page. A five-chair shop is five barbers with their own booking.
The walk-in queue is its own line. It's the thing walk-in shops actually want.
Keep every monthly add-on below the price of two haircuts, or it's cut the first slow month.
Sell the back-to-school page in July and the groomsmen page in January.

lineItems.description: Max with the barber's own cut gallery, specialties and a direct booking link.
Max with a per-barber queue, text alerts when the chair is close and a wait display for the shop screen.
Max when every style has its own entry, guard lengths, and the barber's own cut pictures once shot.

lineItems.item: Cut club membership page and billing
lineItems.description: Max with several membership levels, beard add-ons and recurring billing on their payment account.
Max with a group size form, on-location fees and a deposit to hold the date.
Max with booth rent terms, shop photos once shot and an application form.
Max when the menu, policies and queue messages are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile management for the barbershop
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Correct hours, fresh fade pictures every week and replies to every review, so the barbershop is the one guys nearby actually click."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 0 alongside the build. For most shops this is the real sale.

whatElseYouSell.name: Booking setup for every barber chair
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each barber gets their own calendar, cut menu and hours in the booking app, set up properly once, instead of a shared mess."
whatElseYouSell.when: At build. Often sold before the site is.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each haircut
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "An hour after the haircut, while the fade still looks fresh, the customer gets a text asking for a review of their barber."

whatElseYouSell.name: Barbershop content morning
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One slow morning shooting the chairs, the barbers at work and a few willing regulars' cuts gives the shop a season of posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on the slowest weekday morning.

whatElseYouSell.name: Back-to-school haircut push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A late-summer push to parents for kids' haircuts, spreading the back-to-school rush across the whole week at the barbershop."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in July, run in August.

whatElseYouSell.name: Window decal and barber business cards
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A window decal with hours and the queue code, and a card for each barber, so a good haircut turns into the next booking."

whatElseYouSell.name: Weekly post planning for the barbershop
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "You cut, I plan the week's barbershop posts: open chairs, fresh fades and the Saturday wait."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if nobody in the shop posts consistently.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The supply house where your barbers buy clippers and blades has a phone-only order line. Introduce me and I'll build the order and class page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply houses sell to every barbershop in the region. Their customer list is your prospect list.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The barber school your guys came from sells cheap cuts on the student floor and books them by phone. A booking page fills those chairs."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Schools need practice heads and enrolments. Alumni barbers are trusted introductions.

withoutAI.route: Tattoo shops on the same block
withoutAI.whoPays: The tattoo shop, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The tattoo shop next to the barbershop shares half your customers and still takes requests by DM. I'd build theirs next."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Neighbouring shops refer and see each other's pages daily.

withoutAI.whoPays: The tailor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The tailor who fits your customers' wedding suits books fittings by phone. A page with fitting slots and your barbershop's groomsmen offer helps both."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Grooms visit the tailor and the barber in the same month. The barber's word opens the tailor's door.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The local beard oil maker whose bottles sit on your barbershop counter sells mostly at markets. A shop site and a stockist list would grow that."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small makers rely on barbers to sell their products. The barber is their best reference.

withoutAI.route: Wedding venues that host groom prep
withoutAI.whoPays: The venue, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The venue where your barbers do groomsmen cuts on site needs a vendor page that lists them. I build venue pages too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Venues refer the vendors they trust. A barber who's worked their groom suite is that vendor.

withAI.route: Order-status chat for the barber supply house
withAI.pitchLine: "Barbers ask whether their clipper blades or guards are in stock or ready for pickup and get an answer from the supply house inventory at any hour."
withAI.whyItWorks: Supply houses answer stock questions all day. An assistant tied to their own system takes the easy ones.

withAI.route: Practice-head booking assistant for barber schools
withAI.pitchLine: "The barber school's assistant explains student haircut prices and supervision and books people into open chairs when instructors are on the floor."
withAI.whyItWorks: Schools need a steady flow of practice heads and can count the result in filled chairs.

withAI.pitchLine: "Wedding parties text the tailor their dates and sizes, and the assistant books fittings and suggests the barbershop's groomsmen slot the same week."
withAI.whyItWorks: Tailors juggle group fittings by phone. A booker that also sends business to the barber keeps both happy.

withAI.route: Stockist reorder texts for the grooming product maker
withAI.pitchLine: "Barbershops that stock the maker's beard oil get a reorder text when they usually run out, and reply with quantities to place the order."
withAI.whyItWorks: Reorders are where small makers lose sales. Barbershops prefer a text to a form.

withAI.route: Groom-day schedule builder for the wedding venue
withAI.pitchLine: "Couples enter the ceremony time and party size, and the venue's planner lays out barber, hair and makeup slots from its own vendor list."
withAI.whyItWorks: Venues want the morning of the wedding to run on time. The barbershop is the first vendor on the list.

withAI.route: Request sorter for the tattoo shop next door
withAI.pitchLine: "The tattoo shop next to the barbershop gets its DM requests sorted by size and budget with a draft reply, the way your queue sorts walk-ins."
withAI.whyItWorks: Same block, same customers. They've seen your setup and want their version.

softwareAI.name: Live wait board for the shop screen
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The TV in the barbershop shows who's next for each barber, and the same list is live online for guys deciding whether to walk over."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build, alongside the queue. Needs a screen in the shop and each barber's name.

softwareAI.name: No-show fee for booked haircuts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A booked haircut holds a card, and a no-show on a Saturday chair pays a small fee instead of nothing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 14, or the first time they complain about no-shows. Needs their no-show rule and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Rebooking text at each customer's cut interval
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A guy who gets a fade every two weeks gets a text from his barber on day twelve with open chairs."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs visit history from the booking app and each barber's text wording.

softwareAI.name: Text and DM answerer for the barbershop
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'You open?', 'how much for a cut and beard' and 'what's the wait' get answered from the barbershop's real menu and queue."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the priced menu, hours and queue access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Phone answering while the barbers cut
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The barbershop phone rings over the clippers and nobody can grab it. Now it gets answered, the question handled and the chair booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs menu, hours and booking access. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Cut club billing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Members pay monthly for their haircuts, the barber sees who's a member at check-in, and nobody counts punches on a card."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the membership rules and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for the barbershop
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every barbershop review gets a short reply in the owner's voice naming the barber, ready to send from a phone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the Google profile management. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Lapsed customer text from the barber
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A regular who hasn't sat in the barber's chair for two months gets a short text from him, not a coupon blast."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs visit history and an opt-out line.

softwareAI.name: Booth rent due-date tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For barbershop owners renting chairs: who owes booth rent this week, who's paid, and a polite reminder that sends itself."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, only for shops renting chairs. Needs the renter list and rent terms.

softwareAI.name: Barber commission and tip report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For shops paying commission: each barber's cuts, tips and product sales added up at the end of the week."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, only for commission shops. Needs pay rules and booking data.

softwareAI.name: Caption drafts for fade and beard posts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Post a fresh fade and get a caption with the cut named, the barber tagged and the next open chair mentioned."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a few past captions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Haircut notes per customer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Guard numbers, part side and how he likes the neckline saved per customer, so any barber in the shop can give him the same haircut."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, for multi-barber shops. Needs a habit of noting the cut at checkout.

softwareAI.name: Style match from a reference picture
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A customer uploads the haircut he wants, and the barber gets the closest style name from the shop's fade guide to confirm in the chair."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, once the fade guide is live. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Slow-hour chair fill texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tuesday at two the barbershop is empty, so regulars who opted in get a text that chairs are open now."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs booking data showing the slow hours and an opt-in list.

softwareAI.name: Grooming product shelf and reorder list
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Know which pomades, beard oils and combs sell at the barbershop counter and get a reorder list before the shelf's empty."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, only if they sell retail. Needs product list and sales records.

softwareAI.name: Wait time estimator per barber
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The queue learns how long each barber takes for a fade versus a cut and beard, so the posted wait is close to the truth."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after a couple of months of queue data. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Picture-day and holiday haircut reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Parents get a reminder to book kids' haircuts before school picture day and the holidays, while chairs are still open."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the local school calendar and a list of parents who opted in.

softwareAI.name: Bilingual reply drafts for the barbershop
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Questions about haircuts come in English and Spanish; replies are drafted in whichever the customer used, in the barber's tone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, for shops with a bilingual clientele. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Two-shop numbers board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For owners with a second barbershop: cuts, waits, no-shows and barber hours side by side for both shops."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, only when they open a second location. Needs booking exports from both.

softwareAI.name: Chair renter application screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Barbers applying for an open chair get the same questions, and the owner gets a short summary of each one's experience and cut work."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they have a chair to fill. Needs the owner's must-haves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the queue and rebooking texts for independent barbers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a walk-in queue and rebooking texts for one barbershop. Every barber with a chair and a phone needs the same two things."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Barbers are many, small and talk to each other. A cheap monthly tool spreads shop to shop.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your barbershop's corporate page doesn't show your own barbers or your wait. I build local pages franchisees are allowed to run."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Franchisees want local visibility inside brand rules. One approved template sells to every location.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Graduate launch kit for barber schools
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every new barber leaves school with a page, a priced menu and booking ready the day he's licensed."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Schools sell careers. A kit for every graduating class is recurring and fills your pipeline.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member shop a barbershop page template with a queue and a licensing line as a member benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons; one deal reaches many shop owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency takes on barbershops and builds them like restaurants. License my template with the queue and fade guide built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the shop; you sell them the barber-specific part.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Barber finder for a clipper and trimmer maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your sponsored barbers need a place customers can find and book them. A barber finder tied to your education events does it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Tool makers invest in barber education and want it to reach customers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your barber expo sells tickets and battle entries from a flyer. A site with registration, the class schedule and vendor booths sells more."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Organisers sell to every barber in the region. Your shop's barbers attend and vouch for you.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Stockist map for a men's grooming product brand
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Customers want to buy your pomade where they get their haircut. A stockist map sends them to the barbershops that carry it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Grooming brands sell through barbers and want reorders. A map helps both.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your building rents private suites to barbers. A directory of every barber with live booking, plus a leasing page, fills both chairs and suites."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Suite owners need tenants and tenants need customers. One building is many barbers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your programme runs blood pressure check days in barbershops. A sign-up page per shop with dates and reminders makes every event easier to fill."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Community health programmes already partner with barbershops and need simple sign-ups. The barber client is a partner shop.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same barbershop setup in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New barbershops in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Barbers across the county line keep asking who set up this shop's walk-in queue. They don't cut your customers, so they get the same setup."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template and the finished barber proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your booking app has three barbers who left still taking appointments. I'll clean it up and rebuild each chair's calendar properly."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Shops with a broken setup already pay for the app. Fixing it is a fast, small yes.

upsellLadder.offer: Barbershop page build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The barbershop page and the care plan go on one contract, so a new barber or a price change is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Google profile management for the barbershop
upsellLadder.trigger: Their Google listing still shows wrong hours or old pictures after launch.
upsellLadder.line: "The page is right, now let's make the barbershop's Google profile match it every week."

upsellLadder.trigger: The booking app shows regulars stretching past their usual cut interval.
upsellLadder.line: "Your regulars get a haircut on a rhythm. Let's text them on time and ask for a review while the fade's fresh."

upsellLadder.trigger: They have regulars who come in every couple of weeks and pay cash each time.
upsellLadder.line: "Your every-other-week regulars are already members. Let's bill the cut club monthly."

upsellLadder.offer: Phone answering while the barbers cut
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention missing calls on busy Saturdays.
upsellLadder.line: "Saturday calls nobody can answer over the clippers get picked up and booked."

upsellLadder.trigger: The barber chair pages still show placeholders.
upsellLadder.line: "One slow morning fills every barber's page with real cuts."

upsellLadder.offer: Introduction to the barber supply house
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a supply rep asking who set up the barbershop's booking.
upsellLadder.line: "Your supply house sells to every barbershop around here. Would you introduce me?"
